1. Heard.
2.
Under challenge is the summoning order dated 30.03.2024 passed by learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sitapur, in Complaint Case No.5303 of 2022 in re: Vishram vs. Jitendra etc..
By the said order, the applicants have been summoned for an offence under Sections 498A and 306 IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

3. While raising a challenge to the said order, the argument of learned counsel for the applicants is two folds namely (a) that the death is said to have occurred in Haryana as such the provisions of Jitendra @ Ankit And Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. Home ... on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178797031/
1 Section 202 of Cr.P.C. would have to be followed, and (b) as the offence under Section 306 IPC is triable exclusively by the Court of Sessions consequently all witnesses should have been produced and examined as per the mandatory provisions of Section 202 Cr.P.C. proviso.

sentences.text: 4. However, considering that the summoning order has been issued and the applicants have a remedy of filing of a discharge application as such the instant petition is disposed of leaving it open to the applicants to file an application for discharge taking the aforesaid grounds.

5. It is further provided that in case an application for discharge is filed within a period of two weeks from today by the applicants then the same shall be considered and decided in accordance with law by the learned Court say within a period of four weeks after hearing all the parties concerned provided there is no legal impediment.
6. For a period of two weeks from today, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in pursuance to the impugned order dated 30.03.2024 passed in the aforesaid complaint case.
